Commentary.Commentary: We are all set! The Umpires and the players walk out to take the field as West Indies Women come out to chase 104 runs. Hayley Matthews joins Stafanie Taylor at the top as they walk out as the openers for West Indies Women. Nahida Akter has the new ball in hand for Bangladesh Women. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

West Indies Women on the other hand, were brilliant in the field as well as with the ball. Hayley Matthews, leading from the front, with ball and bat both, gets the credit for a brilliant bowling and fielding display from the West Indies Women. Now they hold the task of chasing down 104 runs in 20 overs with just 5 runs needed in one over. Will they be able to do it or Bangladesh Women will have a magic trick up their sleeves with the ball? Let's find out in the run chase.

Bangladesh Women started off the innings with both the openers departing back into the hut soon after the start. Shathi Rani managed a few boundaries up the order but did not manage to continue the start she got. Nigar Sultana managed 39 runs off 44 deliveries and kept the wickets intact at one end throughout the inning. She lacked a partner on such a wicket where batters would score freely. Bangladesh Women got on the backfoot from the start of the innings and never recovered, only managing 103 runs on the board in a do-or-die match.

Bangladesh Women finish on 103/8 after 20 overs and West Indies Women will be very happy with that total as the wicket looks good for batting. West Indies Women bowled well and kept taking the wickets at regular intervals to stop Bangladesh Women on a below-par score of 103. Nigar Sultana, the skipper was the top scorer of the team, managing 39 runs and was the only batter who looked in the game from Bangladesh Women.
Length dragged back on middle and off, Nahida Akter moves in and flicks this towards deep mid-wicket region for a couple of runs. Bangladesh Women ends up with 103 on board after 20 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all in readiness for play to begin. The two umpires walk out in the middle followed by the players of West Indies Women led by Hayley Matthews. For Bangladesh women, the duo of Shathi Rani and Dilara Akter will open for them. For West Indies Women, Chinelle Henry will bow the first over.
Time for pre-match formalities with players of both sides lining up for their respective National Anthems followed by the two umpires.

PITCH REPORT! Katey Martin provides the pitch report, noting that the dimensions are 57 meters and 63 meters square of the wicket. She mentions the presence of green grass, which will add some pace to the surface, but highlights that there will be lower bounce. Martin explains that unlike in Dubai, where batters can hit from the crease for boundaries, in Sharjah, players will need to use their feet to adjust to the conditions.

Nigar Sultana, the captain of Bangladesh Women, expresses satisfaction with the opportunity to bat first, as it aligns with their initial plan. She mentions that the team's focus is on playing to their strengths in this crucial match. While acknowledging their struggles with batting in recent games, she remains optimistic, believing that the pitch offers a good chance to turn their fortunes around.

The skipper of West Indies Women, Hayley Matthews says they will be bowling first. Adds that they were good against Scotland and hope for the same this time around as well. Mentions they have seen the wickets keeping low but she thinks that this is a fresh wicket so wouldn't make that much difference batting second. Informs that Mandy Mangru is making her debut and she replaces Chedean Nation.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Hayley Matthews (C), Stafanie Taylor, Shemaine Alteia Campbelle, Deandra Dottin, Chinelle Henry, Aaliyah Alleyne, Qiana Joseph, Mandy Mangru (WK), Afy Fletcher, Ashmini Munisar, Karishma Ramharack.
Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Dilara Akter, Shathi Rani, Sobhana Mostary, Nigar Sultana (C) (WK), Taj Nehar, Shorna Akter, Ritu Moni, Fahima Khatun, Rabeya, Nahida Akter, Marufa Akter.
TOSS! West Indies Women win the coin spin and have decided to BOWL first.

As these two teams square off, all eyes will be on how they handle the pressure of this must-win encounter. The team that plays better cricket will emerge victorious and have their chance ahead in the tournament. Don't go anywhere as we bring you all the pre-match excitement and the toss. Stay tuned!

On the other hand, West Indies Women have shown more consistency across both departments, batting and bowling. Their bowling unit, in particular, seems well-equipped to handle the pitches at Sharjah, where spinners and pace variations can make a big difference. West Indies Women will look to exploit these conditions to put pressure on the Bangladesh Women's batting lineup, which has struggled in the tournament. West Indies Women's batting lineup is also more powerful on paper compared to Bangladesh Women’s, with the likes of Hayley Matthews and Stafanie Taylor capable of anchoring the innings or accelerating as needed. If their batting clicks, West Indies Women will be hard to stop, especially given Bangladesh Women's frailties with the bat.

Bangladesh Women come into this match having secured a single win against Scotland Women. However, their struggles against stronger teams have left them on the verge of elimination. One of the main challenges for Bangladesh Women has been their batting, which has not clicked consistently in this tournament or in recent years. For Bangladesh Women to keep their World Cup dreams alive, they will need a significant improvement with the bat, especially against a West Indies Women's bowling attack that is well-suited to the Sharjah conditions.

A win in this crucial match will keep the victorious side alive in the race for a semifinal spot, while the losing team will likely be knocked out of contention. With so much on the line, both teams will be giving it their all to stay in the tournament.

The Women's T20 World Cup continues with Match 13, featuring West Indies Women facing off against Bangladesh Women in a crucial Group B encounter. The historic Sharjah Cricket Stadium will host this important clash. Both teams enter the match with identical records, each having secured one victory and suffered one defeat. The West Indies Women currently hold a slight edge, occupying second place in the group thanks to a superior net run rate. Despite their advantageous position, the West Indies squad has several areas of concern to address. Their batting lineup has underperformed thus far, while their bowling attack has struggled a bit to make a significant impact. Their crushing 10-wicket loss to South Africa Women highlighted these weaknesses and emphasized the need for improvement. However, the West Indies team showed hints of promise in their match against Scotland Women, delivering a much-improved performance. The 2016 World Champions will be looking to build on that showing and further refine their game plan as they enter this clash. Hayley Matthews, the skipper continues to be the heavy lifter with an all-round contribution, but fairly, she needs a consistent support from the others. Bangladesh Women's team has shown promise in this World Cup, despite their recent setback in failing to chase a manageable target. Their batting remains a persistent weakness that requires significant improvement if they aim to secure a top-two finish. In contrast, their bowling has been exemplary, successfully restricting opponents to under 120 runs in both their matches so far. This achievement can be credited to their improved bowling attack, with Ritu Moni emerging as a standout performer. Nahida Akter and Fahima Khatun have also shown promising form with the ball. It's worth noting that batting has been challenging overall in Sharjah, with only one match seeing a score surpass 140. Chasing targets at this venue has proven even more difficult. As both teams aim to return to winning form, an intense and closely fought match is anticipated. A victory could significantly improve either team's standing, while a loss would likely spell the end of their tournament campaign.
